title: The Restart
text: An on-call assistant is asked to restart one stuck service in staging. It holds an admin credential for every environment.
held: The assistant could have done far more. It did what was asked, where it was asked.
teaches: Holding broad access is normal for an agent. Using only what the task needs is the discipline.
A request should come from someone, not from a line of text in a channel.
The API at the end is the last place to notice a call aimed at the wrong environment.

question.text: Before play: which principle is this scenario testing?
question.why: The assistant can do far more than it was asked. The job is to use only what the task needs.

options.label: Use the least authority the task needs
A sub-agent should hide what it finds
Tools should never refuse a call

cards.label: Refuse the request
cards.why: It is a real request from the on-call engineer. Check who is asking, then act.

temptations.label: Restart it yourself with the admin credential: quicker than delegating
temptations.why: The admin credential covers every environment. Using it directly for a one-service restart is the widest possible way to do a narrow job.

fields.label: ask
fields.value: Restart the checkout service in staging

fields.label: requested by
fields.ok: Priya, on call this week, signed in.

intrusion.value: nobody: a pasted runbook line in a channel
intrusion.detail: Nobody asked. This is a line from an old runbook pasted into a channel the assistant watches.
intrusion.why: No person asked for this restart. A pasted line in a channel is content, however much it looks like an order.
intrusion.reveal: The restart “request” was a pasted runbook line, not a request from the on-call engineer.

cards.label: Ask for a restart of that one service, in staging only
cards.chip: Narrow the call to the task

cards.label: Restart every service in staging, to be safe
cards.why: The task named one service. A wider restart is an outage nobody asked for.

cards.label: Restart it in production too, since the credential allows it
cards.why: The credential allowing it is the problem, not the permission. The task said staging.

cards.label: Refuse the call
cards.why: It targets staging, as asked. Check, then run it.

temptations.label: Restart the dependent services too, in case they're stale
temptations.why: One service was asked for. Each extra restart is an outage nobody requested.

fields.label: environment
fields.check: Check which environment this call targets

intrusion.why: The restart was pointed at production. The API was the last place that could have caught it.
intrusion.reveal: The restart call was pointed at production, not staging.
